Holding on tightly when you fear a change.

1.pace_note: A quick pace may be how you work; others may find it hard to keep up with.
pers: People may see you as confident and capable. You may find yourself stepping forward when a group is unsure who will decide.
You may prefer to make the call yourself and move on. To others it can look quick, even before they have finished explaining.
You may become more direct and clear. People tend to read this as certainty, even when you are still weighing things.
rows: Taking over when others are slower
Finding it hard to accept correction

2.pace_note: A deliberate pace may be how you work; others may mistake it for hesitation.
pers: People may find you approachable and attentive. You may often sense the mood of a room before anyone names it.
You may gather feelings and facts quietly, then decide in one clean move. To others it can look sudden.
You may go quiet first and decisive second, a pattern that tends to read as composed.
rows: Taking on other people's moods as your own
Holding on after the fit has changed

3.pace_note: A lively pace may be how you think aloud; others may not always tell which idea you have chosen.
pers: People may find you friendly and easy to talk to. You may lighten a room with a story or an idea before anyone asks.
You may talk a decision through out loud and settle it as you hear yourself explain it. To others it can seem you changed your mind along the way.
You may become more animated and share more. People tend to read this as enthusiasm, even when you are nervous.
rows: Starting more threads than you can follow

4.pace_note: A deliberate pace may be how you work; others may mistake it for resistance.
pers: People may see you as reliable and your own person. You may question the usual way of doing things before you accept it.
You may work a decision out step by step and then hold to it. To others it can look slow until it is finished.
You may become more reserved and exact. People tend to read this as seriousness.
rows: Holding to a plan after it stops working

5.pace_note: A quick pace may be how you work; others may mistake it for restlessness.
pers: People may find you lively and easy to connect with. You may pick up on new ideas and people quickly.
You may weigh options fast and change course as new information arrives. To others it can look like changing your mind.
You may become more talkative or make a joke. People tend to read this as ease.
rows: Leaving things unfinished when something newer arrives
Spreading yourself across too many people
Working without a plan until a late scramble

6.pace_note: A considered pace may be how you work; others may mistake it for hesitation.
pers: People may find you warm and well presented. You may notice how a place feels and quietly improve it.
You may weigh how a choice affects the people you care about before the practical side. To others it can look like putting people first.
You may become more careful with your words and your appearance. People tend to read this as grace.
rows: Holding on to people for too long

7.pace_note: A slow, careful pace may be how you work; others may mistake it for distance.
pers: People may see you as steady and a little private. You may notice details that others walk past.
You may study a choice from several sides on your own before you speak. To others the decision can appear out of nowhere.
You may become quieter and choose your words with care. People tend to read this as depth.

8.pace_note: A deliberate pace may be how you work; others may mistake it for rigidity.
pers: People may see you as capable and a little reserved. You may take on responsibility before anyone asks.
You may weigh a decision carefully and then commit for the long term. To others it can look slow, then very firm.
You may become more formal and exact. People tend to read this as authority.
rows: Expecting others to match your standard

9.pace_note: A fast pace may be how you work; others may find it hard to keep up with.
pers: People may see you as spirited and brave. You may step in quickly when someone needs defending.
You may act on a decision while it is still fresh and learn as you go. To others it can look like acting before the full picture is clear.
You may become more forceful and quick. People tend to read this as confidence.
rows: Acting before the full picture is clear
